title: LCLI-723 round-1 follow-ups: the undeclared-Story carve-out test, 0.2's every-type enum scope, and the untested base.fields empty-enum site
description:
Non-blocking findings from the LCLI-723 review (approved at 10cc270e; PR opum-ai/lore-cli#586). None blocked the merge; all three are gaps in what the change PROVES or SAYS, not defects in what it does.

(2) test/effective-status-enum.test.ts:108 — "the 0.1 task-rollup carve-out survives the precedence change" runs against `customProfile("0.1")`, which declares ONLY `ADR`. A `type: "Story"` document is therefore an UNKNOWN type in that profile, and the carve-out return it exercises is the unknown-type one, not the ADR check: the test proves the carve-out holds for a type the profile does not declare, which is a weaker claim than its name makes. Fix either way — declare a Story in `customProfile("0.1")` and assert the three rollup values pass on a DECLARED type (preferred: that is the claim the name makes), or rename the test to what it actually proves. Note the 0.2 sibling at :47 in the LCLI-669 file uses the BUILT-IN profile, where Story IS declared, so the two files currently demonstrate the carve-out at different strengths.

(3) On OKF 0.2, `validateLifecycleStatus` (src/core/schema.ts:483) judges EVERY type by that type's effective enum; the ADR-only restriction is the 0.1 carve-out, not the 0.2 rule. LCLI-723 made that enum the profile's DECLARED one, so the scope statement is now load-bearing for a custom profile's non-ADR types too. The CHANGELOG's LCLI-723 entry says the change applies "on OKF 0.1 and 0.2 alike" but never states that 0.2's scope is every type. Add one line. MEASURE the sentence against the pinned capacities before landing it: `docs/reference/cli-surface.md` and `cli-contract.md` are declared by several `.lore/agents/*.toml` profiles, and `reference/cli-contract` is PINNED by implementation, review and verification — a CHANGELOG sentence is free (CHANGELOG.md is not a declared source), so put it there and leave the reference pages alone.

(5) NARROWED BY MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-14 — the review reported "no empty-enum load test, although assertNonEmptyEnum exists". There ARE two: test/profile.test.ts:307 pins `types[0].fields.status.enum` and :318 pins a list's `items.enum`. `assertNonEmptyEnum` also refuses at the third declaration site, verified by calling `parseProfile` directly:

    type field enum=[]        -> t: types[0].fields.status.enum must not be empty
    base.fields enum=[]       -> t: base.fields.status.enum must not be empty
    items enum=[]             -> t: types[0].fields.tags.items.enum must not be empty

So the residual gap is the `[base.fields]` site ALONE: it refuses correctly and no test pins it. Worth pinning rather than the other two, because `effectiveLifecycleStatusEnum` (src/core/profile.ts) reads the BASE `status` spec whenever a type declares none — an empty `[base.fields] status = { enum = [] }` is precisely the input the effective-enum path depends on being refused, and nothing currently holds that line.

NOT IN THIS TASK, and deliberately not changed: `superseded_status` is accepted on ANY type (src/core/profile.ts:530) while DEC-192 (6) says "a key on the ADR type". The leader is taking that to opum-doc; a test should pin whichever way it rules, and it is filed separately once the ruling lands.
